title: Walsh character under negated identification
statement: Let $n,m\ge0$, let $z$ and $w$ be Boolean vectors of lengths $n$ and $m$, respectively, let $\pi$ map the $n$ coordinates to the $m$ coordinates, and let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates. Define $O_\pi(S)$ to consist of those target coordinates that have an odd number of preimages in $S$. Form the vector whose $i$th coordinate is $w_{\pi(i)}$ when $z_i=0$ and its complement when $z_i=1$. Its Walsh character on $S$ equals $\chi_S(z)\chi_{O_\pi(S)}(w)$.
hypotheses_covered: $z$ is a Boolean vector of length $n$
$\pi$ maps the $n$ coordinates to the $m$ coordinates
$w$ is a Boolean vector of length $m$
$S$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
replaced:
For $n,m\in\mathbb N$, $z\in\{0,1\}^{n}$, $w\in\{0,1\}^{m}$, a map $\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, define $\chi_A(x)=\prod_{i\in A}(-1)^{x_i}$ for subsets of the coordinate set of $x$, and set $O_{\pi}(S)=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:|\{i\in S:\pi(i)=j\}|\text{ is odd}\}$; then
\[
\chi_S\bigl((z_i+w_{\pi(i)}\pmod2)_{i=1}^{n}\bigr)=\chi_S(z)\chi_{O_{\pi}(S)}(w).
\]
